text:
darren: Heads up — noticed sustained zoning congestion in us-west1 gpu nodepools starting ~00:30 UTC. ClusterAutoscaler kept retrying but hit GCE quota errors and the pod queue backed up. Thinking about a 'spillback' policy to automatically schedule GPU pods into a secondary region (us-central1) when zone capacity or quota errors surface. Thoughts?

olivia: Can you paste the CA logs? want to confirm it's `quotaExceeded` vs tainted nodes. quick grep from logs helped: `ERROR: cloudProvider: failed to create node: googleapi: Error 403: Quota exceeded, quotaExceeded`

sam: ouch. If we start spilling to us-central1 we need to account for cross-region egress + SLO impact. Also reserved/dedicated capacity in us-central is limited. We'll need priority buckets so we don't spill everything and burn committed capacity. :grimacing:

priya: Agreed on buckets. Proposal: 3 priority classes for GPU workloads (critical, best-effort, low-cost). On quota/zone-failure, only critical -> spillback to other region, best-effort -> preemptible instances in same region, low-cost -> queue + backoff. We can implement with podPriority + node affinity + taints. Example patch for nodeSelector affinity on migration: ```apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: ml-infer-critical
spec:
  priorityClassName: critical-gpu
  affinity:
    nodeAffinity:
      preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
      - weight: 100
        preference:
          matchExpressions:
          - key: region-spillback
            operator: In
            values:
            - us-central1
```

olivia: Also we can update ClusterAutoscaler behavior to respect node group priorities and scale up node pools in fallback region only when higher-priority buckets are pending. Config snippet for CA (GKE) to prefer node pools: ```--node-group-auto-discovery=asg:tag=k8s.io/cluster-autoscaler/enabled --expander=least-waste```. But that won't solve quota errors in cloud provider. We'll need preflight checks for quota and a controller that flips a cluster-level annotation `gpu/region-overflow=true` to trigger scheduler predicates.

engbot: Incident summary: gpu-scaling-errors (us-west1) — 27 pods pending for > 2m, error=quotaExceeded, affected nodepools: gpu-pool-x, gpu-pool-y. alert severity: high.

darren: Good catch on controller idea. Outline for rollout: 1) implement priority classes and label fallback nodepools with `region-spillback=us-central1` 2) small controller: watch for quota errors in CA logs -> set cluster annotation + enqueue a SchedulingPolicy CRD 3) scheduler ext plugin honors SchedulingPolicy (spillback TTL 15m) 4) monitor: pending pods count, time-to-schedule, cross-region egress bytes. Start canary on a single service (image-infer-prod) for 48h.

jin: Routing question: do we have existing inter-region VPC routes and peering for traffic? latency to us-central adds 30-60ms median; some models are sensitive. For chat use-cases that's fine, but real-time RL inference might not. Also watch for model weights transfer times if we rely on local disk cache on nodes. Could add a warmpool prefetch step for critical models.

sam: Cost note: spilling critical loads to on-demand GPUs in another region will increase burn. If we use preemptible fallback for best-effort we save money but must handle interruptions gracefully. We should tag spilled events in billing and add cost center to metrics. Suggest adding `spillback.reason` and `spillback.region` labels to pods for chargeback.

priya: Implementation checklist for next sprint (small EPIC):
- create priority classes: critical-gpu, standard-gpu, low-gpu
- label fallback nodepools and expose `region-spillback` label
- small controller: detect CA quota errors, flip cluster annotation, emit event
- scheduler extender / mutating webhook to add affinity when annotation present
- canary rollout + runbook + rollback steps
- dashboards: pending_gpus_by_priority, spillback_count, cross_region_egress_bytes

olivia: We also need a preflight quota probe — run `gcloud compute regions describe us-central1 --project=$P` nightly and alert at 70% of quota for GPUs. If preflight indicates low quota, proactively move low-priority jobs to queued state and warm up fallback pools. Script: ```gcloud compute regions describe us-west1 --format='json(quotas)' | jq '.quotas[] | select(.metric=="GPUS")'```

darren: OK I'll draft the CRD + controller prototype and open PR for priority classes. Can we schedule a quick sync tomorrow 09:30 PT to align on canary service and metrics? tagging: @olivia @priya @sam @jin

engbot: Scheduled meeting created: #infra-ops-sync 2024-11-12 09:30 PT (meeting link).

sam: One more ops concern — network egress firewall and L7 routing needs review. Cross-region calls might hit different ingress controllers; we'll need to validate TLS certs and origin checks for services that verify source region.

priya: Noted. I'll add a pre-canary checklist item: "verify cross-region ingress + certs + origin headers".

darren: Great. If nobody objects I'll push the priority classes PR by EOD and start the controller spike tomorrow. :thumbsup:

olivia: LGTM :shipit:
